# Tokenize + remove stopwords again, now keeping doc_id and label
tokens <- news %>%
  select(doc_id, is_fake, text) %>%
  unnest_tokens(word, text) %>%
  filter(str_detect(word, "^[a-z]+$")) %>%
  filter(str_length(word) >= 3)%>%
  anti_join(stop_words, by = "word")

# Count tokens per article
article_lengths <- tokens %>%
  count(doc_id, name = "n_tokens")

# Minimum-length rule: keep docs with at least 50 cleaned words
min_len <- 50
valid_docs <- article_lengths %>%
  filter(n_tokens >= min_len) %>%
  pull(doc_id)

# Filter to valid articles
tokens_clean <- tokens %>%
  filter(doc_id %in% valid_docs)

3) Data Cleaning and Engineering: Prep for Model

# remove exceedingly long/short articles
max_words <- mean(news$nwords, na.rm=T) + (3 * sd(news$nwords, na.rm=T))
news_filtered <- news %>% filter(nwords >= 10 & nwords <= max_words)
print("Dimensions after filtering by size:", quote=F)
## [1] Dimensions after filtering by size:
dim(news_filtered) # ~1.4k articles removed
## [1] 43544     8
# take sample of articles for memory usability
news_smpl <- news_filtered[sample(nrow(news_filtered), 1500), ]

# form article corpus
news_smpl <- news_smpl %>% select(doc_id, text, title, date, subject, is_fake, nwords) # reorder columns
news_source <- DataframeSource(news_smpl)
news_corpus <- VCorpus(news_source)

# clean corpus text
clean_corpus <- function(corpus) {
  # Remove punctuation
  corpus <- tm_map(corpus, removePunctuation)
  remove_quotes <- content_transformer(function(x) {
    gsub("[“”\"\'‘’`]", "", x) # Removes double quotes, single quotes, and typographic quotes
  })
  corpus <- tm_map(corpus, remove_quotes)
  # remove numbers
  corpus <- tm_map(corpus, removeNumbers)
  # Transform to lower case
  corpus <- tm_map(corpus, content_transformer(tolower))
  # remove contractions
  corpus <- tm_map(corpus, content_transformer(replace_contraction))
  # Remove stopwords
  corpus <- tm_map(corpus, removeWords, words = stopwords("en"))
  # Strip whitespace
  corpus <- tm_map(corpus, stripWhitespace)
  return(corpus)
}
news_corpus <- clean_corpus(news_corpus)

# cast to dtm
news_dtm <- DocumentTermMatrix(news_corpus)
# weight tf-idf
news_tfidf <- weightTfIdf(news_dtm)
# convert to matrix
news_mat <- as.matrix(news_tfidf)

# remove words with near-zero variance of tf-idf
nzv <- nearZeroVar(news_mat)
predictors_reduced <- news_mat[, -nzv]
news_reduced <- cbind(predictors_reduced, is_fake = news_smpl$is_fake)
news_reduced <- as.data.frame(news_reduced)

# seed was not normalized at this point, so these numbers differ slightly from presentation
cat("\nRemoved NZV features:", length(nzv), "\n") 
## 
## Removed NZV features: 31422
cat("Remaining columns:", ncol(news_reduced), "\n")
## Remaining columns: 145

3) Sentiment Analysis

#Getting sentiments
positive <- get_sentiments("bing") %>%
  filter(sentiment == "positive")
negative <- get_sentiments("bing") %>%
  filter(sentiment == "negative")

#Table of positive and negative words in fake/true
amount_pos <- tokens_clean %>%
  semi_join(positive) %>%
  count(is_fake, name = "positive_words")
## Joining with `by = join_by(word)`
amount_neg <- tokens_clean %>%
  semi_join(negative) %>%
  count(is_fake, name = "negative_words")
## Joining with `by = join_by(word)`
#Merge tables to see positive and negative words in each category
amounts <- merge(amount_pos, amount_neg, by = "is_fake")

#Make it long format
amounts_long <- pivot_longer(amounts, positive_words:negative_words,
                             names_to = "word_sentiment", 
                             values_to = "word_count")

#Graphing it
sentiment_analysis <- ggplot(amounts_long, aes(x = is_fake,y = word_count, 
                                               fill = factor(word_sentiment))) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  labs(x = "News Type", y = "Word Count", 
       title = "Negative and Positive Words Per Category")

#Labeling the graph
sentiment_analysis <- sentiment_analysis + guides(fill = guide_legend(title=
                                                                          "Legend")) +
  scale_fill_discrete(labels = c("Negative Words", "Positive Words")) +

sentiment_analysis

## 4) Binary Classification Models

cat("Class balance:\n")
## Class balance:
print(table(news_reduced$is_fake)) # again due to not setting seed prior these numbers differ
## 
##   0   1 
## 728 772
news_reduced$is_fake <- as.factor(news_reduced$is_fake)

# TRAIN / TEST SPLIT
set.seed(123)

train_index <- createDataPartition(news_reduced$is_fake, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)

train <- news_reduced[train_index, ]
test  <- news_reduced[-train_index, ]

x_train <- train %>% select(-is_fake)
y_train <- train$is_fake

x_test  <- test %>% select(-is_fake)
y_test  <- test$is_fake

# Matrix versions for glmnet & SVM
x_train_mat <- as.matrix(x_train)
x_test_mat  <- as.matrix(x_test)

# LOGISTIC REGRESSION (GLMNET) 
log_model <- cv.glmnet(
  x_train_mat, y_train,
  family = "binomial",
  alpha = 0,
  type.measure = "class"
)

log_pred <- predict(log_model, x_test_mat, type = "class")
log_pred <- as.factor(ifelse(log_pred == "1", 1, 0))

log_cm <- confusionMatrix(as.factor(log_pred), y_test)
cat("\n================ LOGISTIC REGRESSION RESULTS ================\n")
## 
## ================ LOGISTIC REGRESSION RESULTS ================
print(log_cm) 
## Confusion Matrix and Statistics
## 
##           Reference
## Prediction   0   1
##          0 142   7
##          1   3 147
##                                           
##                Accuracy : 0.9666          
##                  95% CI : (0.9394, 0.9838)
##     No Information Rate : 0.5151          
##     P-Value [Acc > NIR] : <2e-16

  scale = c(3, 1)
)

blue_palette <- c("#003366", "#004080", "#0059b3", "#3366cc", "#3399ff")
wordcloud(
  words = coefs_df$term,
  freq = abs(-coefs_df$weight),
  min.freq = 0,
  max.words = 100,
  random.order = FALSE,
  colors = blue_palette,
  scale = c(3, 1)
)
